title: Mild chicken tandoori
notes: Mild version: omit chilli and onion. Use lactose-free yoghurt if needed.
ingredients: 600 g chicken thighs or breast, cut into 4–5 cm pieces
method: Cut shallow slits into the thickest parts of the chicken.
Mix yoghurt, oil, spices, garlic, ginger, lemon juice, salt and pepper.
Coat the chicken, cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.
Place on a lined tray and bake at 220°C conventional or 200°C fan for 25–35 minutes, turning once.
Check the thickest piece reaches 75°C. Rest for 5 minutes and serve with rice and sliced cucumber.

title: Chicken biryani
notes: Omit onion and shallots. Add carrots, peas or spinach and keep the spice level mild.
ingredients: 500 g boneless chicken, cut into 4 cm pieces
method: Rinse the rice until the water runs mostly clear. Simmer it in water for 7–8 minutes, then drain while still firm.
Heat rapeseed oil in a large pot and brown the chicken for 4–5 minutes.
Add garlic, ginger, spices, carrots and stock. Simmer covered for 12–15 minutes until the chicken is cooked.
Fold in the rice and peas, cover and cook on low for 8–10 minutes.
Stir through spinach, rest covered for 5 minutes and fluff before serving.

title: Chicken pulao
notes: Leave out onion and keep the spices mild.
ingredients: 500 g chicken breast, cut into 4 cm pieces
method: Heat avocado oil in a heavy pot and brown the chicken for 4 minutes.
Add garlic, ginger, garam masala, rice and stock. Stir once.
Cover and simmer gently for 15 minutes, or until the rice is tender and the chicken reaches 75°C.
Fold in carrots and peas during the final 5 minutes. Rest for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Mild chicken tikka masala
notes: Omit onion and tomato if needed; use mild curry and add spinach.
ingredients: 600 g chicken breast, cut into 4 cm pieces
method: Mix chicken with 75 g yoghurt, half the garlic, half the ginger and the curry powder. Marinate for 30 minutes.
Heat rapeseed oil and brown the chicken in batches for 3–4 minutes.
Add remaining garlic, ginger and stock. Simmer for 12–15 minutes until cooked.
Lower the heat and stir in cream, remaining yoghurt and spinach. Do not boil after adding yoghurt.

title: Easy chicken curry
notes: Use lactose-free yoghurt and add peas or carrots.
ingredients: 500 g chicken, cut into 4 cm pieces
method: Heat oil and brown chicken for 5 minutes.
Add curry powder, garlic and ginger and cook for 1 minute.
Pour in stock and simmer for 15 minutes.
Add carrots and peas and cook for another 6–8 minutes.
Remove from heat and stir in yoghurt.

title: Chicken pad Thai
notes: Keep egg, bean sprouts, peanuts and carrots. Omit spring onion and chilli.
ingredients: 100 g carrot, peeled and cut into matchsticks
method: Soak noodles in hot water until flexible, then drain.
Heat rapeseed oil and stir-fry garlic briefly.
Add noodles, soy sauce and lime juice and toss until hot.
Push noodles aside, scramble the eggs, then combine.
Fold in bean sprouts and carrot for the final minute and finish with peanuts.

title: Chicken teriyaki bowl
notes: Omit spring onion; serve with rice and vegetables.
ingredients: 300 g chicken thighs, cut into 4 cm pieces
120 g carrots, peeled and cut into thin strips
method: Heat oil and brown chicken for 5–6 minutes.
Add teriyaki sauce and simmer until glossy and chicken reaches 75°C.
Steam carrots and peas until just tender.
Serve over rice with vegetables and bean sprouts.

title: Salmon sushi bowl
notes: Use salmon, rice, cucumber, avocado and sesame; skip mayonnaise.
method: Cut salmon into 3 cm cubes.
Bake at 200°C fan for 10–14 minutes until flaky, or pan-cook until the centre reaches 63°C.
Arrange rice, cucumber and avocado in bowls.
Top with salmon, sesame seeds, soy sauce and sesame oil.

title: One-pot chicken and rice
notes: Omit onion and add peas, carrots or corn.
ingredients: 500 g chicken thighs, cut into 4 cm pieces
method: Heat oil and brown chicken for 5 minutes.
Add garlic, paprika, rice and stock and bring to a simmer.
Cover and cook on low for 18–20 minutes.
Add carrots, peas and corn for the final 5 minutes.
Check chicken reaches 75°C and rest for 5 minutes.

title: Chicken fried rice
notes: Keep egg, peas and carrots. Add corn or bean sprouts.
ingredients: 300 g chicken, diced into 2 cm pieces
method: Heat avocado oil and cook chicken with garlic and ginger until done. Set aside.
Scramble eggs in the same wok.
Add carrots, peas and corn and stir-fry for 3 minutes.
Add rice and soy sauce and toss over high heat.
Return chicken and fold in bean sprouts.

title: Biksemad
notes: Use leftover pork or beef. Omit onion and add peas or carrots.
ingredients: 400 g cooked pork or beef, cut into 2 cm cubes
500 g cooked potatoes, cut into 2 cm cubes
method: Heat rapeseed oil.
Fry potatoes for 8–10 minutes until golden.
Add meat and carrots and cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in peas for 2 minutes.
Fry eggs separately and place them on top.

title: Danish frikadeller
notes: Use chicken mince and omit onion.
method: Mix mince, egg, breadcrumbs, milk, salt and pepper and rest for 10 minutes.
Shape into 8–10 meatballs.
Pan-fry in rapeseed oil until browned and the centre reaches 75°C.
Boil potatoes for 15–20 minutes and serve with peas.

title: Salmon traybake
notes: Omit tomato and capers; keep potatoes and asparagus and add peas.
ingredients: 500 g potatoes, cut into 3 cm wedges
method: Toss potato wedges with oil, salt and pepper and roast at 210°C fan for 25 minutes.
Add salmon and asparagus and bake another 12–15 minutes until salmon flakes and reaches 63°C.
Boil peas for 2–3 minutes and serve with lemon.

title: Salmon pasta
notes: Omit capers and onion; use spinach, peas and lactose-free cream.
ingredients: 350 g salmon, cut into 3 cm pieces
method: Cook pasta and reserve 100 ml water.
Cook salmon in rapeseed oil for 4–5 minutes until flaky.
Add cream and peas and simmer for 3 minutes.
Fold in spinach, then toss with pasta, lemon juice and pasta water.

title: Frittata
notes: Use eggs, spinach, peas, corn, asparagus and mozzarella.
ingredients: 150 g asparagus, trimmed and cut into 3 cm pieces
method: Heat avocado oil.
Cook asparagus for 4 minutes, then add peas, corn and spinach.
Pour over beaten eggs and add mozzarella.
Cook gently for 5 minutes, then grill at 200°C for 3–5 minutes until set.

title: Spanish omelette
notes: Omit onion; use potato, egg, peas and spinach.
ingredients: 500 g potatoes, peeled and sliced 3 mm thick
method: Cook potato slices in oil over medium-low heat for 12–15 minutes until tender.
Add peas and spinach for 2 minutes.
Pour over beaten eggs and cook until mostly set.
Finish under a grill until firm and lightly golden.

title: Chicken pasta bake
notes: Use mozzarella; omit tomato and onion and add peas and spinach.
ingredients: 400 g chicken breast, diced into 3 cm pieces
method: Cook pasta until 2 minutes short of tender.
Cook chicken in oil until the centre reaches 75°C.
Combine with sauce, peas and spinach.
Top with mozzarella and bake at 200°C fan for 20 minutes.

title: Chicken wraps
notes: Use lettuce, cucumber, carrots, corn and avocado; no mayonnaise.
method: Warm wraps briefly.
Prepare lettuce, cucumber, carrots, corn and avocado.
Toss avocado with lemon juice.
Fill wraps, fold in the sides and roll tightly.

title: Steak and chips
notes: Use lean steak and oven-baked potatoes; add asparagus or peas.
ingredients: 500 g potatoes, cut into 1 cm chips
method: Toss chips with oil and roast at 220°C fan for 30–35 minutes, turning halfway.
Season steaks and sear in a hot pan for 2–4 minutes per side depending on thickness.
Rest for 5 minutes. Steam asparagus for 4–5 minutes or boil peas for 2–3 minutes.

title: Pork tenderloin traybake
notes: Omit onion; use potatoes, carrots, squash and peas.
ingredients: 500 g potatoes, cut into 3 cm pieces
200 g carrots, peeled and cut into 2 cm pieces
250 g squash, peeled and cut into 3 cm cubes
method: Toss potatoes, carrots and squash with oil, paprika and salt. Roast at 210°C fan for 25 minutes.
Add pork and roast another 18–22 minutes until the centre reaches 63°C.
Rest pork for 3 minutes and serve with peas.

title: Salmon and pea pasta
notes: Use lactose-free cream and omit onion and capers.
ingredients: 350 g salmon, cut into 3 cm pieces
method: Cook pasta and reserve 100 ml water.
Cook salmon in oil until flaky.
Add cream, peas and spinach and simmer for 3 minutes.
Toss with pasta, lemon juice and pasta water.

title: Chicken and avocado rice bowl
notes: A simple bowl using cucumber, corn and avocado instead of heavy dressing.
method: Cook chicken in avocado oil until the centre reaches 75°C, then rest and slice.
Prepare cucumber, carrots, corn and avocado.
Arrange rice and vegetables in bowls.
Top with chicken and lemon juice.

title: Garlic Ginger Chicken
notes: Mild version; omit green onion if preferred. Serve with rice or vegetables.
ingredients: 680 g boneless, skinless chicken thighs, cut into bite-sized pieces
30 ml avocado oil or another high-smoke-point oil
method: Toss the chicken with cornflour and salt until evenly coated.
Heat the oil in a large pan and cook the chicken until golden on the outside and nearly cooked through.
Whisk together the honey, chicken stock and soy sauce.
Add the garlic and ginger to the pan and cook briefly until fragrant.
Pour in the sauce and simmer until thickened and the chicken reaches 74°C internally.
Finish with the sliced green onions and serve with rice or vegetables.

title: Chicken fajita rice bowl
notes: Uses the fajita spice profile without bell pepper, onion or tomato. Add cucumber and avocado after cooking.
method: Toss chicken with oil, paprika, cumin, oregano and salt.
Cook in a hot pan for 6–8 minutes until the centre reaches 75°C.
Divide rice, lettuce, corn, cucumber and avocado between bowls.
Top with chicken and lime juice.

title: Beef picadillo-style potato skillet
notes: A tomato-free version inspired by Latin American picadillo; use carrots and peas for sweetness.
method: Brown the beef in oil for 5–6 minutes.
Add potatoes, carrots, cumin, paprika, oregano, stock and salt.
Cover and simmer for 15–18 minutes until potatoes are tender.
Stir in peas and corn and cook for 3 minutes.

title: Pork carnitas bowl
notes: Serve with rice, cucumber, avocado and corn instead of salsa or beans.
ingredients: 700 g pork shoulder, cut into 5 cm pieces
method: Place pork, stock, orange juice, garlic, cumin, oregano and salt in a pot.
Cover and simmer gently for 75–90 minutes until tender.
Shred the pork and crisp it in a hot pan for 5 minutes.
Serve with rice, cucumber, avocado and corn.

title: Greek-style chicken and potatoes
notes: Tomato-free and onion-free; serve with cucumber and yoghurt.
method: Mix chicken with half the lemon juice, oil, garlic, oregano, paprika and salt.
Arrange chicken, potatoes and carrots on a tray.
Roast at 210°C fan for 40–45 minutes until chicken reaches 75°C and potatoes are golden.
Mix yoghurt with the remaining lemon juice and serve alongside.

title: Beef kofta potato plates
notes: Use cucumber-yoghurt sauce without mint if preferred. No onion is needed.
ingredients: 150 g cucumber, grated and squeezed dry
method: Mix beef, egg, breadcrumbs, cumin, coriander, paprika and salt.
Shape into 12 small kofta and place on a tray with potatoes tossed in oil.
Bake at 210°C fan for 20–25 minutes until kofta reach 71°C and potatoes are tender.
Mix cucumber, yoghurt and lemon juice and serve with the kofta.

title: Salmon with lemon couscous
notes: Add spinach, cucumber or peas. Couscous is measured dry.
method: Place couscous in a bowl, pour over boiling stock, cover and stand for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork.
Season salmon with paprika and salt and bake at 200°C fan for 12–15 minutes until flaky and 63°C in the centre.
Fold spinach, cucumber, lemon juice and oil through the couscous.
Serve salmon over the couscous.

title: Chicken spinach mozzarella pasta
notes: A tomato-free pasta bake using melted mozzarella.
method: Cook pasta until just under al dente and reserve 100 ml water.
Cook chicken in oil with garlic, basil and salt until it reaches 75°C.
Stir in cream, spinach and pasta water.
Combine with pasta, top with mozzarella and bake at 200°C fan for 15 minutes.

title: Beef and spinach tagliatelle
notes: Tomato-free beef pasta with a light yoghurt finish; do not boil after adding yoghurt.
method: Cook the tagliatelle and reserve 100 ml pasta water.
Brown beef in oil with garlic, paprika, oregano and salt.
Add stock and spinach and simmer for 3 minutes.
Remove from heat and stir in yoghurt, then toss with pasta and enough pasta water to coat.

title: French-style chicken with carrots and peas
notes: A simple tomato-free and onion-free creamy chicken stew.
ingredients: 600 g chicken thighs, cut into 4 cm pieces
method: Brown chicken in oil for 5 minutes.
Add carrots, stock, thyme, bay leaf, salt and pepper.
Cover and simmer for 20 minutes until chicken reaches 75°C.
Add peas and cream and cook gently for 5 minutes. Remove bay leaf before serving.

title: Shawarma chicken plate
notes: Serve with rice, cucumber and yoghurt sauce; omit onion and tomato.
method: Mix chicken with yoghurt, lemon juice, oil, spices, garlic and salt. Marinate for 30 minutes.
Cook in a hot pan for 8–10 minutes until browned and the centre reaches 75°C.
Serve with rice and cucumber, using extra yoghurt as a sauce if desired.

title: Lamb-free chicken shawarma wraps
notes: Uses chicken because it is milder and fits your preferences. No tahini or mayonnaise required.
method: Toss chicken with oil, spices, garlic and salt.
Cook in a hot pan for 6–8 minutes until the centre reaches 75°C.
Mix yoghurt and lemon juice.
Fill wraps with lettuce, cucumber, avocado, chicken and yoghurt sauce.

title: Beef gyudon-style rice bowl
notes: Onion-free adaptation. Add cucumber or spinach on the side.
method: Simmer stock, soy sauce, mirin and sugar for 3 minutes.
Add beef and cook for 3–4 minutes until just cooked.
Poach or fry the eggs separately.
Serve beef and sauce over rice with spinach and egg.

title: Korean-style beef rice bowl
notes: Omit onion and pear if desired; use cucumber and carrots as fresh toppings.
method: Mix soy sauce, sesame oil, honey, garlic, ginger and pepper.
Coat beef and marinate for 20–30 minutes.
Stir-fry beef in batches over high heat for 3–5 minutes.
Serve with rice, cucumber and carrots.

title: Jerk chicken with rice and peas
notes: Use ordinary peas rather than kidney beans; adjust chilli to taste.
method: Coat chicken with oil, jerk seasoning, garlic, lime juice and salt.
Bake at 210°C fan for 30–35 minutes until the centre reaches 75°C.
Warm rice with peas and carrots.
Serve chicken with the rice mixture.

title: Jamaican-style beef and potatoes
notes: A mild, tomato-free stew with warming spices.
ingredients: 600 g stewing beef, cut into 3 cm cubes
method: Brown beef in oil in batches.
Add stock, allspice, paprika, thyme, garlic and salt.
Cover and simmer for 75–90 minutes until tender.
Add potatoes and carrots and cook for 20 minutes, then add peas for 3 minutes.

title: Pulled pork potato bowls
notes: Use barbecue sauce without onion or tomato if needed, or season with paprika and honey instead.
method: Place pork, stock, paprika, honey, vinegar and salt in a covered ovenproof pot.
Cook at 160°C conventional for 2½–3 hours until tender.
Shred pork and crisp it briefly in a pan.
Roast potatoes at 220°C fan with oil for 30–35 minutes and serve with corn and cucumber.

title: Apple cinnamon yoghurt oats
notes: A simple breakfast using oats, yoghurt and fruit.
method: Mix oats, yoghurt, milk, grated apple, honey and cinnamon.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Top with banana and pumpkin seeds before serving.

title: Berry yoghurt oat bowl
notes: Use any preferred berries or other fruit.
method: Divide yoghurt and oats between bowls.
Top with berries, banana and almonds.
Drizzle with honey and sprinkle with cinnamon.

title: Spinach, potato and mozzarella bake
notes: A meat-free option using vegetables you already enjoy; no tomato, onion or mushrooms.
method: Boil potato slices for 6 minutes and drain.
Layer potatoes, spinach, peas, garlic, salt and pepper in a baking dish.
Pour over cream and top with mozzarella.
Bake at 200°C fan for 30–35 minutes until potatoes are tender and cheese is golden.
